what: Śaiva ascetic institutions, maṭhas and sites in Karnataka that passed from Kālāmukha to Vīraśaiva hands

evidence.detail: Proposed in modern scholarship (e.g., D. N. Lorenzen's study of the Kāpālikas and Kālāmukhas) that the Kālāmukhas were absorbed into the Vīraśaiva movement; labeled scholarly metadata.
Neither Vīraśaiva account of origins mentions the Kālāmukhas; Allama's birthplace Baḷḷigāve was a known Kālāmukha centre (inscriptions; moderate confidence).

notes: Recorded as a borrowing, not a dispute, because no tradition text debates it; see dsp:virasaiva-origins.

what: The twenty-eight Śaiva Āgamas (Kāmika to Vātula) as scripture, with Vīraśaiva doctrine located in their later portion; Vīraśaiva recensions of the Candrajñāna and Makuṭa Āgamas

evidence.detail: SSM 1.25–27 and 5.14 name the Āgamas from Kāmika to Vātula as the source.

what: The vocabulary of full I-ness (pūrṇāhantā), supreme I-ness and this-ness (idantā) for the state of union
era: by the time of the SSM

evidence.detail: SSM 14.38–41 uses pūrṇāhantā, parāhantā and idantā.

what: Veneration of the Tamil Nāyaṉmārs as purātanas, the models of devotion for the śaraṇas

evidence.detail: Harihara's ragaḷes and the Basava Purāṇa narrate the lives of the purātanas.

what: The ninefold devotion (śravaṇa, kīrtana, smaraṇa…), re-addressed to Śambhu
era: by the time of the SSM

evidence.detail: SSM 9.2–3 parallels Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5.23 ('śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ viṣṇoḥ…') with Śambhu in place of Viṣṇu.

what: Upaniṣadic images of the self and the light
era: by the time of the SSM

evidence.detail: SSM 12.38 echoes Kaṭha 5.15 / Muṇḍaka 2.2.10 / Śvetāśvatara 6.14; 18.6 echoes Śvetāśvatara 5.9; the SSM's commentary cites the Upaniṣads throughout.

what: Yogic anatomy — the bulb (kanda), prāṇa and apāna, six centres, the thousand-petalled lotus and the moon at the crown — integrated into Śivayoga

evidence.detail: Direction of influence between Vīraśaiva Śivayoga and haṭha/tantric yoga is not settled.
